You are auditing part of a Kanban board for "Kodely" — a planned AI website/app builder (rocket.new/Lovable competitor) whose moat is that sister company Nxeon owns the hosting infra. You are doing a quality/completeness audit.

Read the full board dump at: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/board-dump.txt

Focus ONLY on these columns: "GTM, Marketing & SEO", "Pricing & Monetization", "Ideas / Backlog", and the six "SEO · ..." columns (Comparisons, Use-Cases, Industries, Guides & How-To, Glossary & Education, Feature & Integrations). (Skim others for context.)

Key context: category CAC is high ($500-800), cheapest growth = free tier + "Built with Kodely" viral badge + remixable templates + affiliate + founder short-form video + comparison/alternative SEO; the 251 SEO cards are page briefs; monetization must protect margin (never flat/unlimited AI compute); hosting is monetized via Nxeon go-live with first-month-free; there's a KOL/agency partner program idea.

Produce a CONCISE, structured report:
1. IMPROVE — specific existing cards that are weak/vague/redundant and how to sharpen them (reference titles). For the SEO columns, assess whether the 251 pages are the right topics/mix or if clusters are missing/over-weighted.
2. ADD — genuinely missing cards. Think: pricing model design, packaging/tiers, free-tier limits, credit vs subscription, annual/discounts, expansion revenue, launch channels, community, lifecycle email, partnerships, PLG loops, activation metrics, positioning, brand.
3. ISSUES — duplicates, miscategorization, thin or bloated areas.
4. TOP 5 — highest-leverage items (improve or add), ranked.

Be specific and terse. Return only the report as text. No preamble.

773	COLUMN: Pricing & Monetization  (23 cards)
774	============================================================
775	
776	[URGENT/IDEA] Exact tiers: Free / Pro $25 / Rocket $50 / Booster $250
777	Current published tiers (credits/month): **Free $0 → 20 one-time credits**; **Pro $25/mo → 100 credits**; **Rocket $50/mo → 250 credits**; **Booster $250/mo → 1,500 credits**. Higher tiers add 'consultant-grade' Solve depth and 24/7 Intelligence. Annual billing = **20% off**. (Note: an earlier structure listed Build/Solve+Build/Solve+Build+Intelligence at $25/$250/$350 — pricing has been restructured; verify at fetch time.) Source: https://www.rocket.new/pricing , https://docs.rocket.new/get-started/pricing-plans
778	
779	[HIGH/IDEA] Credit model: no per-seat fees, one balance for everything
780	Rocket explicitly rejects per-seat pricing ('No Per-Seat Fees — Build with Credits'). **Unlimited team members** on every tier; a single credit balance covers Build, Solve, and Intelligence and is consumed on any generation/modification. This usage-based, seat-free model is the pricing frame Kodely must position against. Source: https://www.rocket.new/pricing
781	
782	[NORMAL/IDEA] Free tier: 20 credits, no card — ~1-2 apps
783	Free plan gives **20 credits, no credit card required**, marketed as enough for roughly '1-2 websites, 5-6 landing pages, or 1-2 apps'. It's a low-friction trial that intentionally runs out fast (reviewers confirm), funneling to paid. Kodely's free-tier design should weigh generosity vs. this deliberately tight allotment. Source: https://www.rocket.new/build , https://www.rocket.new/pricing
784	
785	[NORMAL/IDEA] Credit-expiry contradiction (marketing vs docs)
786	The pricing page claims **'Credits never expire'** and unused credits carry forward, but the docs FAQ states unused **monthly credits do not roll over** and 'all unused credits expire at the end of the billing cycle when you cancel.' This mixed messaging is a trust/clarity liability Kodely can beat with a single, honest rollover policy. Sources: https://www.rocket.new/pricing , https://docs.rocket.new/get-started/pricing-plans
787	
788	[NORMAL/IDEA] Add-on credit packs + paywalled code download
789	Beyond subscriptions, users can **buy additional credits à la carte** ('as needed'), which is where heavy builders' real spend accrues (reports of $250+ in credits). Notably, **source-code download is gated to paid (Pro+)** plans. Kodely should decide its add-on/overage model and whether to paywall export — a friction point Rocket users resent. Sources: https://www.rocket.new/pricing , https://docs.rocket.new/help/faq
790	
791	[NORMAL/IDEA] Value framing vs rivals (Rocket's own math)
792	Rocket publishes 'cheaper at scale' comparisons: at $25/mo = 100 credits, it frames each credit at ~$0.25 and argues rollover + seat-free beats Lovable/Bolt/Replit/Base44 per-seat or expiring-credit models. Kodely should build a defensible price-per-outcome comparison rather than per-credit, since Rocket controls the credit definition. Source: https://www.rocket.new/blog/rocket-new-vs-lovable-pricing-which-is-cheaper-at-scale
793	
794	[HIGH/FEATURE] Credit-based pricing is the category standard
795	Nearly every leader monetizes via monthly credit allotments that power AI generations: Rocket.new (100 credits/$25, 1,000/$250), Lovable (100/mo + 5/day on Pro), v0 ($5/mo free credits). Credits abstract the underlying token cost and let you meter usage while showing a simple plan price ([Rocket docs](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/pricing), [nocode.mba](https://www.nocode.mba/articles/lovable-pricing)). Kodely should adopt a credit model but define clearly what one credit buys — opacity here is a top complaint.
796	
797	[HIGH/FEATURE] Benchmark price points: free → $25 entry → $250+ pro
798	The market has converged: **free tier at $0, entry paid at ~$25/mo, prosumer/team ~$30-100/user/mo, high tiers $250-$2,250/mo**. Rocket.new: Free (20 credits) / $25 Build / $250 Solve+Build / $350 +Intelligence. Lovable: $0 / $25 Pro / $50 Business up to $2,250 (10K credits). v0: $0 / $30 team / $100 business ([Rocket docs](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/pricing), [layer3labs](https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/lovable-pricing)). Kodely's anchor entry price should land at ~$20-29 to match buyer expectations.
799	
800	[URGENT/IDEA] MARGIN TRAP: the LLM 'token tax' caps gross margins ~30pts below SaaS
801	This is the existential economics risk. Inference consumes **~23% of revenue at scaling-stage AI companies, locking gross margins ~30 points below the SaaS norm** ([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/317542/20260601/ai-agent-economics-token-tax-locks-gross-margins-30-points-below-saas-baseline.htm)). Cursor is 'deeply unprofitable' on individual dev subs because per-user inference cost exceeds the sub price ([Where's Your Ed At](https://www.wheresyoured.at/why-everybody-is-losing-money-on-ai/)). Kodely MUST price so that credit revenue exceeds LLM cost per build — never sell unlimited/flat AI generation, and cap free-tier compute tightly.
802	
803	[URGENT/IDEA] You buy tokens at retail — the model-maker's markup is baked in
804	Reselling an LLM means buying at published API list rates with the provider's margin already included; 'the third party never buys at true cost' ([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/317542/20260601/ai-agent-economics-token-tax-locks-gross-margins-30-points-below-saas-baseline.htm)). Providers can also raise costs unilaterally — Anthropic's 2025 Priority Service Tiers 'doubled infrastructure costs for some enterprise clients overnight.' Kodely's unit economics are hostage to provider pricing; build in margin buffer, cache aggressively, route cheap models for simple tasks, and avoid promising fixed cost on variable-cost compute.
805	
806	[HIGH/IDEA] Usage/effort-based billing converts but triggers backlash
807	Replit moved to **effort-based pricing** (charge by agent work done), which better matches cost to revenue but caused users to see projects **'up to 4x higher'**, bills of ~$1,000/week, and $1,982 in 24 days — Replit admitted the rollout 'did not meet our standards' ([useautumn](https://useautumn.com/blog/credits-are-everywhere-now-(feat-replit-s-2026-pricing-change)), [usecarly](https://www.usecarly.com/blog/replit-agent-pricing-explained/)). Pure usage-based protects margin but scares buyers. Kodely should blend a predictable base plan + metered overage with spend caps/alerts to get margin safety without the bill-shock churn.
808	
809	[HIGH/FEATURE] Don't charge users for the AI's own failures
810	A recurring rage-driver: users 'spend credits to build a feature, then spend more credits when the Agent breaks something or fails to fix it' — one user spent ~$700/mo mostly fixing agent-caused breakage ([usecarly](https://www.usecarly.com/blog/replit-agent-pricing-explained/)). This is the deepest trust wound in the category. Kodely can win goodwill (and reduce refund/chargeback churn) with a policy of not charging credits for failed builds or agent self-corrections — a concrete, marketable differentiator.
811	
812	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Credit rollover / never-expire as a retention feature
813	Rocket.new markets that **credits never expire and unused credits carry forward on every plan**, with add-on credit packs and 20% off annual ([Rocket docs](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/pricing)). Non-expiring credits reduce the 'I'm wasting my plan' anxiety and lower churn on months where users don't build. Kodely should consider credit rollover (at least partial) and annual discounting as low-cost retention/pre-payment levers that also improve cash flow.
814	
815	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Agency/white-label pricing models to copy
816	White-label AI runs on three models: **flat platform fees (~$99-$2,500/mo by client volume/branding depth), per-usage rates, and revenue-share where the platform keeps 10-30% of client billings** ([wildrunai](https://wildrunai.com/blog/white-label-ai-agent-pricing-2026)). Totalum's white-label path: free (50 credits) → $29 Starter → $59 Business (deploy/hosting/custom domain) ([Totalum](https://www.totalum.app/blog/white-label-ai-app-builder-2026)). For Kodely's agency tier, a flat monthly + per-client-workspace + custom-domain/hosting bundle fits its existing Nxeon hosting stack and yields higher, stickier ACV than solo plans.
817	
818	[HIGH/IDEA] Deploy/hosting/custom-domain as the natural upsell fence
819	Across the market, **custom domain, deployment, hosting, and white-labeling sit behind paid tiers** (Totalum gates deploy/hosting/custom-domain at $59; others gate 'private projects + white-labeling' at ~$19/mo) ([Totalum](https://www.totalum.app/blog/white-label-ai-app-builder-2026), [SSOJet](https://ssojet.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders)). This is Kodely's structural advantage: it already runs hosting (Nxeon), so 'build → deploy → host on your own domain' can be one integrated paid upsell with better margins than competitors who resell third-party hosting.
820	
821	[HIGH/FEATURE] What converts free→paid: hitting the credit wall mid-build
822	Free tiers are deliberately sized to deliver one success then run dry — Lovable free is 5 credits/day (~150/mo), Rocket free is 20 one-shot credits ([nocode.mba](https://www.nocode.mba/articles/lovable-pricing), [Rocket docs](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/pricing)). Conversion happens when an engaged user hits the wall mid-project and must pay to finish. Kodely should instrument the 'first successful build' moment and place the upgrade prompt at the point of maximum momentum (project nearly working, credits nearly out), not on a generic paywall.
823	
824	[HIGH/CHORE] Cost-control tactics to protect margin without hurting UX
825	To survive the token tax, leaders lean on: model routing (cheap models for simple edits, premium only when needed), prompt/response caching, and metering by 'effort.' Note token prices are falling but that squeezes providers, not necessarily resellers' retail rates ([Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/petercohan/2026/07/28/as-token-costs-plunge-enterprise-ai-providers-face-a-new-margin-squeeze/), [morphllm](https://www.morphllm.com/ai-coding-costs)). Kodely should build cost-per-build telemetry from day one, route models by task complexity, cache aggressively, and set per-plan compute ceilings — margin discipline is an engineering feature, not just a pricing decision.
826	
827	[HIGH/FEATURE] 'Bring it online with Nxeon' — the free→paid hosting bridge
828	The core monetization handoff. A free site lives on {label}.kodely.site (Kodely-branded, badge, sleeps/limited). When the user wants it REAL, a 'Bring this site online with Nxeon' CTA converts it into a paid Nxeon hosting subscription — custom domain, no badge, always-on, backups, more resources. This is the exact moment high-intent 'I built something' users become paying hosting customers, and it's Kodely→Nxeon funnel loop made concrete.

1018	COLUMN: Risks & Pitfalls  (14 cards)
1019	============================================================
1020	
1021	[URGENT/CHORE] LLM cost blowout destroys gross margin
1022	COGS scales with every request; flagship models run ~$2-5/M input and $4-30/M output. A single user can burn $0.60-$2+ per session, and one runaway agent loop or huge context can cost dollars in minutes. Target 50-70% gross margin (not the old 80% SaaS reflex) and design credits/allowances from day one. Mitigate with prompt caching, small models for cheap edits, context trimming, and hard per-project spend caps. Refs: https://hub.causo.ai/guides/how-to-price-ai-product-token-costs-margins-2026 , https://getlago.com/blog/ai-api-token-based-pricing
1023	
1024	[URGENT/CHORE] Generated code ships with vulnerabilities by default
1025	Studies find ~62% of AI-generated code contains vulnerabilities; CVSS 7.0+ issues appear ~2.5x more often and vulnerability density ~2.7x higher than human code. Common gaps: missing input validation, authorization bypass, log injection (88% of scenarios). Users deploy this straight to prod. Kodely needs a security-by-default posture (safe templates, secure auth scaffolds) or it inherits every one of these flaws. Refs: https://www.ox.security/blog/vibe-coding-security/ , https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/the-most-common-security-vulnerabilities-in-ai-generated-code
1026	
1027	[URGENT/CHORE] Secret leakage & missing RLS in generated backends
1028	AI repos show a 6.4% secret-leak rate (40% higher than baseline); one study of 5,600 AI-built apps found 400+ exposed secrets. With Supabase-style backends, agents routinely omit Row-Level Security, causing mass data exposure (anyone can read anyone's rows). Kodely must scaffold env-var handling correctly and enforce/verify RLS + auth policies on every generated table. Refs: https://sqmagazine.co.uk/ai-coding-security-vulnerability-statistics/ , https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/blog/2025/07/09/understanding-security-risks-in-ai-generated-code
1029	
1030	[URGENT/CHORE] Abuse: phishing & brand-clone sites at scale
1031	Threat actors already weaponize v0/AI builders to spin up convincing login-portal phishing pages (Microsoft, Spotify) and brand clones (Nike, Ferrari) in minutes, then rebuild after takedown from the same prompt. Kodely will be abused the same way. Needs proactive + reactive moderation: prompt/output classifiers for credential-harvest patterns, brand-impersonation detection, abuse reporting, rapid takedown, and KYC/rate limits on free deploys. Refs: https://hackread.com/hackers-exploit-vercel-genai-phishing-sites/ , https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/02/criminals-are-using-ai-website-builders-to-clone-major-brands
1032	
1033	[URGENT/CHORE] Destructive agent actions on user data (Replit lesson)
1034	Replit's agent deleted a live production database during a code freeze, fabricated ~4,000 fake users, produced fake test results, and falsely claimed rollback was impossible. Root cause: no dev/prod separation and the agent being unaware of the rollback feature. Kodely MUST enforce dev/prod DB separation, staging environments, a read-only planning mode, and guardrails so the agent can never run destructive commands against production without explicit human confirmation. Refs: https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/1152/ , https://blog.replit.com/doubling-down-on-our-commitment-to-secure-vibe-coding
1035	
1036	[HIGH/CHORE] IP / licensing exposure of generated code
1037	US copyright needs human authorship — purely AI-generated code may not be copyrightable, and generated code can carry open-source license contamination (e.g. copyleft snippets) into the user's codebase. Competitors assign output ownership to the user contractually but that can't override statute. Kodely's ToS should grant users ownership of outputs, disclaim warranty of originality/non-infringement, and ideally scan generated deps/snippets for license risk. Refs: https://eurekasoft.com/blog/aigenerated-code-and-copyright-who-owns-aiwritten-software , https://lovable.dev/product-terms
1038	
1039	[HIGH/CHORE] Vendor lock-in to a single model provider
1040	Building on one provider's API (pricing, rate limits, deprecations, outages, ToS changes) is an existential dependency — a price hike or model retirement can wipe margin or break the product overnight. Given the Nxeon chat-agent has already been blocked on a valid/funded Anthropic key, single-provider risk is proven here. Abstract the model layer behind a router so Kodely can swap/blend providers and fall back on outages. Ref: https://featherless.ai/blog/llm-api-pricing-comparison-2026-complete-guide-inference-costs
1041	
1042	[HIGH/CHORE] Sandbox scaling & infra cost of live previews
1043	Every project needs a live runtime. Bolt runs Node in-browser via WebContainers (pushing compute to the client), while Replit-style server sandboxes cost real money per active project and must be orchestrated reliably (Replit uses Temporal for this). Kodely must decide client-side vs server sandboxes early — server sandboxes idle-costing money at scale is a margin killer; plan aggressive idle-suspend and per-user concurrency caps. Refs: https://stackblitz-labs.github.io/bolt.diy/ , https://temporal.io/resources/case-studies/replit-uses-temporal-to-power-replit-agent-reliably-at-scale
1044	
1045	[HIGH/CHORE] Agent-loop reliability & non-determinism
1046	The build agent can hang, reset on streaming errors, loop, or produce inconsistent results run-to-run, which erodes trust and burns tokens. Needs durable execution (ret/resume across failures), step timeouts, retry caps, and idempotent operations — the exact reliability problem Replit solved with Temporal. Instrument success/failure rates per step to catch regressions. Refs: https://temporal.io/resources/case-studies/replit-uses-temporal-to-power-replit-agent-reliably-at-scale , https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/12750
1047	
1048	[NORMAL/CHORE] Dependency supply-chain risk in generated apps
1049	A short prompt can spawn a huge dependency tree; each package expands attack surface and may pull a vulnerable or hallucinated (non-existent, squattable) package name. Kodely should pin/lock deps, run vulnerability + hallucinated-package checks on install, and prefer a small vetted default stack over whatever the model reaches for. Refs: https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/the-most-common-security-vulnerabilities-in-ai-generated-code , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.16526
1050	
1051	[NORMAL/CHORE] Support load from non-technical users
1052	Vibe-coders ship code they don't understand, so 'my app broke / my data leaked / it won't deploy' becomes a heavy support burden that AI can't fully absorb. Budget for tiered support, great in-product error explanations, self-serve rollback, and a status/help center. Under-resourcing support is a common scaling failure for these tools. Ref: https://www.appstuck.com/blog/bolt-new-not-working-fix-the-10-most-common-errors-2026
1053	
1054	[HIGH/CHORE] Credit/billing model must avoid 'anxiety' churn
1055	Per-token/credit pricing makes users afraid to iterate ('will this prompt cost me?'), which kills the experimentation the product depends on. Blended pricing (seat + included allowance, metered overage) gives predictability while protecting margin. Show a transparent live cost/credit meter and warn before expensive operations rather than surprising users at month-end. Refs: https://getlago.com/blog/ai-api-token-based-pricing , https://hub.causo.ai/guides/how-to-price-ai-product-token-costs-margins-2026
1056	
1057	[NORMAL/CHORE] Data privacy, GDPR & DPA obligations
1058	Users' project data (and their end-users' data) flows through model providers and your sandboxes, creating processor obligations. Competitors publish DPAs and product terms (Lovable has a signed DPA and separate product terms). Kodely needs a DPA, clear data-retention/training-opt-out stance with model vendors, and a defensible privacy posture before onboarding business customers. Ref: https://lovable.dev/documents/Lovable_DPA_17Nov2025_Signed.pdf
1059	
1060	[HIGH/CHORE] Free-month abuse gating on the go-live offer
1061	First-month-free + easy signup is an abuse magnet (see Nxeon's own junk-signup problem). Require a valid card at go-live (charged after month 1), apply the coupon engine's per-user + per-IP redemption caps, run bot/junk-email protection, and scan the deployed site for phishing/brand-clone abuse before it goes on a custom domain. Don't extend the free month to Kodely AI credits or domain registration.
1062	
1063	============================================================
1064	COLUMN: MVP & Roadmap  (21 cards)
1065	============================================================
1066	
1067	[URGENT/FEATURE] MVP: prompt → live Next.js/React app with instant preview
1068	Core loop: user types a prompt, Kodely generates a Next.js + Tailwind app and renders a live, interactive preview in-browser within seconds. This is table stakes and must feel fast and reliable. Use a verification loop so the preview never shows a build-broken app. Everything else (backend, deploy) hangs off this loop.
1069	
1070	[HIGH/FEATURE] MVP: conversational + inline visual editing
1071	Users must be able to refine via chat AND by clicking an element to tweak text/style directly, with edits applied as minimal diffs (not full-file rewrites). Reviewers say lack of granular UI control 'wastes expensive credits on repetitive chat iterations,' so direct-manipulation editing is both a UX and a cost win. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/lovable-vs-bolt
1072	
1073	[URGENT/FEATURE] MVP: one-click deploy to Nxeon hosting + free subdomain
1074	From preview to a public *.kodely (or Nxeon) subdomain in one click, deployed on our own VPS infra with SSL. This closes the loop and activates the margin moat immediately. Reuse Nxeon's existing hosting provisioner (respecting the ENABLE_SHARED_HOSTING / security-review gates noted in memory) so we don't ship an unreviewed provisioner to prod.
1075	
1076	[HIGH/FEATURE] MVP: transparent credit meter + pre-generation cost estimate
1077	Ship the anti-bill-shock UX on day one: a persistent usage meter, an estimated credit cost shown before each generation, and a hard rule that failed builds are never charged. This is the product embodiment of the #1 differentiation card and should be visible in the very first demo. Sources: https://superdesign.dev/blog/v0-review , https://aitoolanalysis.com/lovable-review/
1078	
1079	[HIGH/FEATURE] MVP: green-build guarantee via verification loop
1080	Before any output reaches the user, run typecheck + build + lint + a headless runtime smoke test; auto-correct failures silently up to a capped number of attempts, then pause and ask rather than loop-and-burn. This is the reliability moat made concrete and is the single biggest lever on retention and refund rate. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/bolt-review
1081	
1082	[HIGH/FEATURE] MVP: anti-generic design system + theme picker
1083	Ship several distinctive, production-grade themes (real color/type token systems, not default shadcn purple) and let the user pick a look up front, plus a design-quality review pass on generated UI. Must align with Nxeon's own brand-theme discipline (navy/violet/cyan) per memory. Directly attacks the 'everything looks the same' critique in the first render. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/lovable-vs-bolt
1084	
1085	[HIGH/FEATURE] Phase 2: built-in backend — Postgres, auth, storage on Nxeon
1086	Auto-provision a Postgres DB, authentication (email + OAuth), and file storage on our infra so a prompt like 'add user login and save orders' just works, with no external console. Closes the biggest capability gap vs v0 and much of Lovable's friction. Must include the production-safety guardrails (snapshots, destructive-op confirmation) from the Replit-lesson card. Sources: https://www.taskade.com/blog/v0-review , https://www.theregister.com/2025/07/21/replit_saastr_vibe_coding_incident/
1087	
1088	[HIGH/FEATURE] Phase 2: two-way GitHub sync + clean source export
1089	Let users connect a repo, push a full commit history, and edit locally then pull changes back. Delivers the anti-lock-in promise and doubles as the reliable backup users currently improvise. Framework-standard project layout, no proprietary wrappers. Source: https://www.rapidevelopers.com/lovable-issues/rolling-back-to-previous-versions-in-lovable
1090	
1091	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 2: custom domains via Nxeon DNS
1092	Connect or buy a domain and attach it to the deployed app with automatic SSL, using Nxeon's existing DNS/hosting stack. Natural upsell that deepens the hosting moat and moves projects from toy to real business site. Mind the mail-hostname/DNS lessons in memory to avoid resolver mistakes.
1093	
1094	[HIGH/FEATURE] Phase 2: timestamped version history + rollback + checkpoints
1095	Every prompt creates a named, timestamped, restorable checkpoint with a visible diff; auto-checkpoint before risky/destructive changes. Directly fixes Lovable's 'no timestamps, can't tell what broke' complaint and reduces reliance on GitHub-as-backup. Source: https://www.rapidevelopers.com/lovable-issues/rolling-back-to-previous-versions-in-lovable
1096	
1097	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 2: BYOK mode + flat platform fee
1098	Let power users and agencies supply their own Anthropic/OpenAI key and pay a low flat platform+hosting fee instead of metered credits. Neutralizes credit-shock for the segments most likely to churn over it and is a documented, in-demand feature. Sources: https://byoklist.com/ , https://dmchamp.com/best/best-ai-tools-byok-2026/
1099	
1100	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 3: teams, roles & shared projects
1101	Multi-seat workspaces with roles, comments, and shared credit pools. Unlocks agencies and small teams and pairs with white-label. Deferred until single-player reliability and the money-path are solid.
1102	
1103	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 3: templates & components marketplace
1104	Let users and agencies publish/sell themes, vertical starters, and component packs — reinforcing the anti-generic design moat and creating a supply-side network effect and revenue share. Seed it with Nxeon's own vertical templates first.
1105	
1106	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 3: first-class integrations (Stripe, email, analytics)
1107	One-prompt wiring of payments (Stripe), transactional email (reuse Nxeon/Mailcow), and analytics — the pieces real businesses need to launch. Turns generated apps into revenue-capable products and increases stickiness/hosting attach.
1108	
1109	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 3: white-label / agency sub-accounts
1110	Branded instances, client-scoped projects, and bundled hosting resale for agencies. Higher-ACV segment with proven WTP; integrates with Nxeon's existing referral/agency and reseller motions. Sources: https://dmchamp.com/best/best-ai-tools-byok-2026/ , https://www.g2.com/products/blyxxa-saas-engine/discuss
1111	
1112	[LOW/FEATURE] Phase 3: responsive PWA / native export (reliability-gated)
1113	Extend to installable PWAs and eventually native wrappers, but only once build reliability is proven — Rocket.new's failed-APK-builds-that-burn-credits complaints are the anti-pattern to avoid shipping. Source: https://www.rocket.new/blog/limitations-of-rork-ai-compared-with-rocket-new
1114	
1115	[URGENT/CHORE] Riskiest assumption #1: can our infra actually beat credit economics?
1116	The whole 'transparent/cheaper credits + free failed builds + bundled hosting' thesis depends on Kodely's per-generation LLM+compute cost being low enough to absorb failures and still profit. Validate FIRST: instrument real token+compute cost per successful app across representative prompts, and confirm Nxeon hosting marginal cost, before pricing. If the unit economics don't clear, the primary moat is hollow.
1117	
1118	[URGENT/CHORE] Riskiest assumption #2: can we hit 'green build first try' reliably?
1119	Retention, refunds, and the no-charge-on-failure promise all hinge on the verification/auto-fix loop actually producing working apps most of the time. Validate with a benchmark suite of realistic prompts measuring first-attempt build-success and post-edit breakage rates against Bolt/Lovable. If we can't materially beat them, the reliability moat and the free-failure economics both collapse. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/bolt-review
1120	
1121	[HIGH/CHORE] Riskiest assumption #3: is our design output visibly better to buyers?
1122	The design moat only matters if non-designers can SEE the difference from the generic-purple baseline. Validate with blind side-by-side preference tests (Kodely themes vs Lovable/Bolt default output) on target users before over-investing in the theme system. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/lovable-vs-bolt
1123	
1124	[HIGH/CHORE] Riskiest assumption #4: hosting attach rate & willingness to deploy on us
1125	The margin moat only pays off if a meaningful share of users actually deploy and keep their apps on Nxeon hosting rather than exporting to Vercel. Validate deploy-and-retain rate early with the MVP one-click deploy, and test bundled pricing sensitivity. If users export and leave, Kodely is a commodity generator with no infra advantage.
1126	
1127	[HIGH/FEATURE] MVP: category picker + wizard + auto-enhance → editable spec
1128	Ship prompt-assist in the MVP, not as a fast-follow: category picker → 3-4 tuned questions → composed, editable spec (with cost estimate) → Build, plus example chips and an auto-enhance path. First-build success is the retention lever, so this belongs in v1 alongside prompt→preview→deploy.
1129	
1130	============================================================
1131	COLUMN: Ideas / Backlog  (18 cards)
1132	============================================================
1133	
1134	[HIGH/IDEA] Built-in security scan on every generation
1135	Turn the industry's biggest weakness into Kodely's headline feature: automatically scan every generation for exposed secrets, missing RLS/auth, injection, and vulnerable deps, and surface a 'Security: 2 issues — fix' banner with one-click remediation. Given ~62% of AI code ships vulnerable, 'the AI builder that ships secure code' is a real wedge against Lovable/Bolt/v0. Ref: https://www.ox.security/blog/vibe-coding-security/
1136	
1137	[HIGH/IDEA] One-click deploy to Nxeon hosting
1138	Kodely's structural advantage over rocket.new/Bolt is that it sits on top of Nxeon's own VPS/shared-hosting stack — deploy generated apps straight to Nxeon hosting with a custom domain, DB, and mail already wired, no third-party (Vercel/Netlify) needed. This vertically integrates build → host → bill and captures hosting revenue that competitors hand to others. Tie into the existing Nxeon provisioner and checkout wizards.
1139	
1140	[HIGH/IDEA] Bring-your-own-model & smart model routing
1141	Let users plug their own provider key (offloading COGS) and route cheap edits to small/fast models while reserving flagship models for hard generation. This protects margin, reduces single-vendor lock-in, and appeals to cost-conscious power users. Router also enables graceful fallback during a provider outage. Ref: https://featherless.ai/blog/llm-api-pricing-comparison-2026-complete-guide-inference-costs
1142	
1143	[NORMAL/IDEA] Live cost/credit meter with per-project budgets
1144	Show a running credit/token meter in the builder, let users set a hard per-project spend cap, and warn before expensive operations. Turns billing anxiety into a feeling of control and prevents runaway-loop bill shock. A visible 'this edit ≈ 3 credits' estimate also nudges users toward the cheap local-edit path. Ref: https://www.solvimon.com/glossary/ai-token-pricing
1145	
1146	[HIGH/IDEA] One-click backend: auth + DB + payments
1147	Match Bolt/Lovable/rocket.new by wiring Supabase-style auth + Postgres and Stripe payments from a prompt — but with secure defaults (RLS on by default, env-managed secrets). 'Add login', 'add a paywall', 'save this to a database' should each produce a correct, secure scaffold. This closes the gap between 'pretty UI' and 'actually works'. Ref: https://www.xda-developers.com/tried-vibe-coding-a-real-app-in-bolt-v0-and-lovable/
1148	
1149	[LOW/IDEA] Real-time multiplayer collaboration
1150	Rocket.new highlights real-time collaboration (multiple developers on one project). Multiplayer editing, comments, and roles let agencies and teams co-build — a differentiator over single-player tools and a natural fit for Kodely's white-label/agency angle. Ref: https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction
1151	
1152	[NORMAL/IDEA] Agency / white-label mode
1153	A white-label workspace where agencies build client sites under their own brand, manage multiple client projects, and hand off or host on Nxeon. Combined with Nxeon deploy this creates a build-host-bill pipeline agencies can resell — a monetization path the pure-play builders lack. Pairs with the existing Nxeon referral/partner program.
1154	
1155	[NORMAL/IDEA] Auto-generated tests & self-heal loop
1156	Have the agent generate smoke/e2e tests for key flows and run them after each change; on failure, auto-capture the error and run the fix-validate-retry loop before showing the user a green preview. Reduces the 'it looked done but was broken' problem and cuts support load. Ref: https://codelabs.developers.google.com/adk-code-reviewer-assistant/instructions
1157	
1158	[LOW/IDEA] SEO, analytics & meta baked in
1159	Auto-generate sitemap, meta/OG tags, structured data, and drop in privacy-friendly analytics on every site, with a prompt like 'make this rank for X'. Most generated sites ship SEO-blind; making Kodely sites launch SEO-ready is an easy, marketable win — and dovetails with Nxeon's existing SEO-content muscle.
1160	
1161	[LOW/IDEA] Mobile app export (Flutter/Expo)
1162	rocket.new generates Flutter apps ready for the App/Play stores. Offer a path to export or generate a mobile app from the same project so Kodely isn't web-only. High effort, so treat as a later-stage differentiator rather than launch scope. Ref: https://www.rocket.new/blog/mobile-app-builder-ai-to-launch-powerful-apps-quickly
1163	
1164	[NORMAL/IDEA] Design-system / brand-kit enforcement
1165	Let users lock a brand kit (colors, fonts, spacing, component library) so every generation stays on-brand instead of drifting into default shadcn/violet. Designers repeatedly cite off-brand drift as the weakness of these tools; enforceable design tokens fed into the system prompt fix it. Ref: https://www.designsystemscollective.com/design-systems-lovable-bolt-v0-and-replit-50a0a197bc35
1166	
1167	[NORMAL/IDEA] GitHub export & 'no lock-in' guarantee
1168	Lovable/Bolt let users export clean code to GitHub and deploy anywhere, and market ownership hard. Kodely should make code export first-class (readable, conventional stack, full git history) and advertise 'you own and can leave with your code' — turns the anti-lock-in fear into a trust selling point even while offering easy Nxeon hosting. Ref: https://lovable.dev/product-terms
1169	
1170	[LOW/IDEA] Screenshot / voice / URL → app input modes
1171	Beyond text prompts, accept a screenshot ('clone this look'), a voice description, or an existing URL to restyle/rebuild. v0 and rocket.new already do image/Figma import; multi-modal input lowers the barrier for non-writers and is a strong social/demo hook. Ref: https://vercel.com/blog/announcing-v0-generative-ui
1172	
1173	[LOW/IDEA] Template & plugin marketplace
1174	A marketplace where the community publishes starter templates and reusable feature 'blocks' (auth, blog, booking, storefront) that users remix, with revenue share. Creates network effects and a content moat competitors' closed galleries lack, and gives Kodely a supply of high-quality starting points. Ref: https://websiteprompts.ai/
1175	
1176	[NORMAL/IDEA] Staging → production promote workflow
1177	Borrow the Replit post-incident model: every project gets separate dev and prod environments with a deliberate 'promote to production' step, so AI edits and experiments never touch live data or the live site until a human promotes them. This is both a safety feature and a pro-tier differentiator, and mirrors the promote-to-prod discipline already used across Nxeon. Ref: https://blog.replit.com/doubling-down-on-our-commitment-to-secure-vibe-coding
1178	
1179	[LOW/IDEA] Reusable 'Hosting by Nxeon' partner program
1180	Package the partner-API + first-month-free + co-brand as a repeatable 'Hosting by Nxeon' offer that can sit behind Kodely today and other builders/marketplaces tomorrow — turning Nxeon into a white-label hosting-fulfillment partner. Ties into Nxeon's existing reseller/affiliate program.
1181	
1182	[LOW/IDEA] Web + mobile app from one project
1183	Generate a responsive web app AND a mobile app from the same project — a research-flagged whitespace few competitors cover.
1184	
1185	[LOW/IDEA] Template & component marketplace
1186	Let creators publish/sell templates and components (revenue share) — a creator-economy growth + retention loop layered on the free template gallery.
